data.prompt: Run your `knapsack` function on the extreme test cases that exercise the boundaries: an empty list of items, a single item whose weight is larger than the capacity, and a capacity of zero. Print the intermediate values of `c` and `c-w` inside the inner loop (e.g., using `print(c, c-w)`). Observe whether any of those index expressions refer to a position outside the `best` list.
data.trace_question: What is the largest (or smallest) value that the expression `c-w` can take during the inner loop for each of the boundary inputs you tried? Does any execution attempt to access `best` at a negative index or at an index equal to `capacity`?
data.expected_insight: The student will see that when `capacity` is 0 (or when `w` exceeds `capacity`), the inner loop still runs and evaluates `best[c-w]` with `c-w` equal to -1, which tries to read `best[-1]` and raises an IndexError, exposing the out‑of‑range index contradiction.
